interpretation: V144 may forecast aggregate next-session risk only. Leader selection probability cannot be claimed improved until V150 specific-theme factors pass a new isolated group walk-forward and complete-trade validation. V161 permits severe-abnormal rule-distance diagnostics only, not a calibrated hit probability or buy ranking. V162/V163 do not authorize a two-to-three-day emotion probability; daily output must remain main/alternative/risk scenarios with invalidation conditions. V164 keeps theme membership separate from catalyst timing and expectation saturation; current theme evidence cannot train or rerank candidates. V158/V190 now govern 64 short-term hypotheses; all remain research-only until isolated out-of-sample tests pass. V166 does not authorize relay cumulative turnover as a ranking factor. V167 does not authorize failed-seal path as a positive ranking factor. V168 prevents secondary theme rosters from being promoted to verified catalyst or high-low evidence. V169 separately verifies business membership, active driver and expectation; verified membership alone remains descriptive and cannot authorize ranking or high-low mapping. V170 keeps first-board and relay cross-theme races in separate lanes and uses same-confidence peers only; current incomplete scope authorizes neither training, winner selection nor entry. V171 separates arithmetic threshold proximity from a fully evidenced path role; the current full-pool replay has zero verified candidate distances and therefore selects neither a closest candidate nor a path-potential candidate. V172 finds a descriptive promotion premium for two-level-or-greater ladder gaps, but middle-damage separation and conditional B+2 evidence are unstable; ladder gaps remain identity context rather than a positive ranking factor. V173 finds that the first turnover board after a one-price streak retains next-day identity premium, but it does not establish a B+2 payoff edge or monotonic benefit from higher turnover; first opening remains delayed-price-discovery risk requiring intraday and theme confirmation. V174 makes all six roles and both group-primary lanes explicit; absent validated evidence, the unique comprehensive result is cash, and the contract itself never authorizes entry. V175 rejects an any-low-stock promotion flag as nearly constant and uses realized lane promotion-rate dominance only for scenario review; it cannot be leaked into the prior close or authorize a high-to-low trade. V176 corrects Level-1 auction semantics and freezes a minute propagation-order contract, but no real forward observations exist; neither net matched-amount change nor event order proves cancellation intent, causal feedback, stock ranking, or entry. V177 separates broad from narrow profit distribution: a positive mean with a non-positive median cannot upgrade the environment by itself. Its aggregate historical scenario is descriptive and cannot rerank stocks or authorize entry. V178 separates clean and fragile breadth expansion; its full-sample and validation directions agree, but discovery and validation intervals do not both pass. It may be displayed as a repair-quality warning, not used as an emotion gate, stock ranker, or entry. V179 finds no monotonic next-session deterioration from aggregate one-price-board share and only eleven formal-consensus sessions. One-price share may describe crowding, delayed price discovery, and buyability, but cannot be a direct emotion gate or entry signal. V180 extends breadth quality to aggregate B+1/B+2/B+3 market paths; recent validation is adverse for fragile expansion, but discovery intervals cross zero. Only an uncalibrated scenario warning is allowed, never a candidate holding-period or entry inference. V181 rebuilds highest-anchor buyability with no-touch rows and next-session one-price rows retained as negatives. The identity/emotion/price-volume challenger does not beat the boards-only baseline, so height identity cannot support a candidate probability, automatic relay primary, stock reranking, or entry. V182 separates opening strength from post-fill payoff. Above-7% opens show materially more one-price unbuyability, while payoff advantages between bands are not stable. Opening gap is available only at 09:30, cannot enter the prior-close model, and no band can authorize stock reranking or entry without intraday and theme confirmation. V183 conditions the opening-gap tradeoff on supportive, hot, and adverse emotion groups. Payoff effects do not replicate across time segments, so emotion cannot waive the above-7% risk flag, create an automatic veto, rerank stocks, or authorize entry. V184 retains every low-open candidate in the opening denominator. Conditioning on later limit touch inflates the validation B+2-positive rate by about 10.6 times and uses future information; low opens are neither automatic buys nor automatic rejects and require live reclaim, VWAP, volume, and theme confirmation. V185 separates daily first-board supply from individual promotion odds. The at-least-one-promotion event is nearly constant, while high supply has no stable positive candidate edge; breadth cannot upgrade emotion, rerank stocks, or authorize entry. V186 shows that promotion identity is not buyable B+2/B+3 payoff: most promoted names fail the full-denominator buyable B+2-positive path. Promotion probability cannot replace separate buyability, payoff, big-loss, or complete-trade targets. V187 separates a broad repair close from proven next-session follow-through. The recent validation segment is directionally better, but discovery and validation intervals cross zero; repair quality can frame a scenario only and cannot provide a calibrated relapse probability, emotion gate, stock reranking, position, or entry. V188 separates first-board, middle-board, and height-layer repair transmission. Middle confirmation loses its discovery advantage in validation, and only three recent sessions confirm all layers; layer structure cannot become a hard emotion gate, positive stock factor, position-size increase, or entry signal. V189 separates an aggregate healthy high-to-low ecology window from collapse-masked low-layer strength. Recent direction does not replicate in development, and no specific-theme stock identity exists; the window cannot select a supplement, create a same-theme mapping, increase position size, or authorize entry. V190 separates first-board new-cycle attention from relay height attention. High relay share does not stably suppress first-board payoff, while high first-board supply is adverse to relays only in the recent segment. Lane supply is context only: it cannot create a common winner score, replace specific-theme evidence, rerank a stock, or authorize entry.
